# Introduction to Nuclear and Particle Physics {.hero-title}

Lectures by Prof. Dr. Mikhail Mikhasenko at Ruhr-Universität Bochum.
From quantum mechanics and the constituents of matter to interactions,
experiments and particle kinematics.

## Lectures {.section-title}

Browser slides with interactive demonstrations. Press **F** for full screen,
**Esc** for the overview. Films require an internet connection.

:::: {.lecture-grid}
::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 1 · Introduction]{.card-tag}

### Nuclear and particle physics

Particle tracks, quantum mechanics, spin, the Standard Model and its interactions.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_1/Lecture_1.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_1/Lecture_1.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_1.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 2 · Kinematics]{.card-tag}

### Particle kinematics

Four-momentum, reconstructed mass, two-body decay, boosts and production thresholds.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_2/Lecture_2.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_2/Lecture_2.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_2.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 3 · Amplitudes]{.card-tag}

### Quantum amplitudes and transition rates

Recap of Relativity and natural units; Mandelstam variables,
resolution, conservation laws, oscillations and widths, angular momentum,
Fermi’s golden rule.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_3/Lecture_3.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_3/Lecture_3.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_3.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 4 · Rates]{.card-tag}

### Decay rates and cross sections

Phase space and normalization, Particle decays with two- and three-body kinematics,
cross sections, luminosity, and
differential cross sections.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_4/Lecture_4.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_4/Lecture_4.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_4.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 5 · Matter]{.card-tag}

### Interaction of particles with matter

Recap of phase space, cross sections and luminosity; ionization, the TPC,
bremsstrahlung and multiple scattering.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_5/Lecture_5.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_5/Lecture_5.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_5.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 6 · Matter]{.card-tag}

### Interaction of particles with matter

Ionization review, bremsstrahlung, multiple scattering, photon and nuclear
interactions, Cherenkov light, and a 3D time projection chamber.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_6/Lecture_6.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_6/Lecture_6.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_6.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 7 · Detectors]{.card-tag}

### Particle detectors I

Recap of interactions with matter; magnets and momentum, gas detectors, silicon
sensors, scintillators and photosensors, and a momentum-resolution explorer.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_7/Lecture_7.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_7/Lecture_7.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_7.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 8 · Accelerators]{.card-tag}

### Particle accelerators

Why accelerate, electrostatic machines and RF cavities, magnets and focusing,
emittance, synchrotron radiation, and six interactive demos from a voltage
ladder to a collider designer.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_8/Lecture_8.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_8/Lecture_8.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_8.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 9 · Trigger and DAQ]{.card-tag}

### Basics of trigger and data acquisition

From Tycho Brahe's logbook and the first Geiger-counter coincidences to a
DAQ built step by step, dead time, the LHC pipeline and two trigger levels,
with a calorimeter-trigger exercise and two interactive demos.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_9/Lecture_9.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_9/Lecture_9.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_9.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 10 · Dirac equation]{.card-tag}

### The Dirac equation

Equations of motion from Newton to Maxwell to fermions, the γ matrices and
four-component spinors, solutions at rest and in motion with the 2E
normalization, and two pictures of antiparticles, with an interactive spinor explorer.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_10/Lecture_10.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_10/Lecture_10.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_10.pdf"}
:::

::: {.course-card}
[Lecture 11 · Feynman rules]{.card-tag}

### Feynman rules and the trace technique

QED Feynman rules, spin sums and traces leading to the lepton tensor,
cross sections for e⁻μ⁻ → e⁻μ⁻ and e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻, helicity at the QED vertex,
and a bridge back to Rutherford scattering, with an interactive cross-section explorer.

[Open slides](slides/lectures/Lecture_11/Lecture_11.qmd){.btn-main}
[Download PDF](slides/lectures/Lecture_11/Lecture_11.pdf){.chip download="Lecture_11.pdf"}
:::
